entry.title: [miladdokhanchi] For complex human problems, we shouldn't be looking for technical answers! If a…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @miladdokhanchi

For complex human problems, we shouldn't be looking for technical answers! If a pipe in your house bursts, that's a technical problem; but when your neighbor puts their trash out earlier than they're supposed to, that's no longer merely technical — it belongs to the realm of human problems. In teaching problem-solving, the first thing we draw the learner's attention to is distinguishing the technical problem from the human problem, and when we talk about problem-solving and teaching it, we mean the second category — because technical problems require expertise in their own field. If my phone stops working, I go to a specialist and they fix it. But human problems don't necessarily have predetermined solutions, and technical expertise alone won't help solve them. The solution to these problems has to be discovered, and solving them requires a basic understanding of the humanities and learning the skill of problem-solving. The biggest mistake is usually offering technical solutions for problems with human roots. When my employees' motivation is low and they show up late to work because of it, I can't force them into line with punishment, incentives, and a few new rules; I need to ask why their motivation has dropped, invite them into a conversation, and address the problem at the level of human relationships. Another mistake is assuming that our technical expertise can help us solve human problems — which it absolutely cannot. Yet another mistake is framing problems with human roots in technical terms. In that same example of lateness, if I say the reason is that they wake up late and that a morning phone call will get them to work on time, I've framed a human problem in technical terms! Mistaking technical problems for human ones and vice versa, offering technical solutions for human problems, and expecting clear technical solutions for complex problems — these are among the greatest plagues of our country's decision-making and problem-solving system. In this regard, the Iranian opposition abroad is hardly innocent either! We Iranians don't have strong problem-solving skills, and at the root of this situation you can feel the hegemony of engineers and physicians, the failure of humanities scholars to engage with concrete problems, and the jurists who want to solve human problems through technical legislation. This pattern shows itself when Hezbollahis are waiting for the leadership to solve the problem, the general public is waiting for the government, and some are waiting for Trump! Oblivious to the fact that solutions are discovered in small settings, and top-down solutions are all doomed to fail. Governments never have solutions for anything, and when they do, they're technical solutions for complex human problems. #Government-Addiction

entry.title: [miladdokhanchi] Why don't the gatherings have their former fervor? Hossein Ghadyani: May God…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @miladdokhanchi

Why don't the gatherings have their former fervor? Hossein Ghadyani: May God not forgive the negligence and fault of the founder and orchestrator of the Stability Party. The late Mesbah or anyone else. In my writings, I refer a lot to Mesbahism, but a more concrete example of the disaster the Stability [Party] people brought upon the revolution is the nighttime gatherings. Gatherings that in the first nights were truly national have now become a haunt for Mesbah's agents and devotees, so that instead of speaking to us of Khamenei's oppression, they speak of the oppression of blogger-representatives or child-representatives. When I write about Mesbahism, I don't only mean the Stability Party. Many are not members of this party but in their politicking have the same method and manner. A few nights ago I was in Mashhad. Those gatherings that I saw with my own eyes, the discussion of hijab was raised in them more than Iran. The speakers were all in the style of Resaei. So what enthusiasm does such a gathering leave for me? Were we supposed to defend Iran under the code name of Khamenei, or ramble about the necessity of the Protection Plan? Mesbahism has brought upon the nighttime gatherings the same disaster it brought upon the revolution. With tricks, they reduced the number of our country's tricolor flag and replaced it with purely red flags of blood-seeking. Night before last, in one of the gatherings in Tehran, slogans against Khatami and Rouhani were more than slogans against Trump and Netanyahu. Was the goal to reach this point? Then they say why don't you participate in the gatherings? Well, you have turned the gatherings into a hangout of Mesbahists. With the same style of reasoning that speaks of the necessity of trying Rouhani, Ahmadinejad and Jalili must also be tried. Look at the output of Mesbah's Velayat Plan classes. Master-playing and Ammar-showing. Did Ahmadinejad not stand before His Excellency the Leader many times with insolence? Why don't people like Sabeti and Raeifipour and Jebraeili and other Mesbahists incite the Hezbollahis to chant against Ahmadinejad? Is it not in their interest? It was the oppressed Khamenei who asked Mesbah to fill Motahhari's empty place, but Mesbah placed partisanship above purification and also knows the delusional art of playing the role of Beheshti. The output of the Islamic Republic Party was the martyred Deylami, and the output of the Stability Party is the deceitful Resaei, who later of course split from Stability. The irony is that the group calls itself one day Deylami and another day Modarres. The problem of the front of the revolution is not Resaei, for Resaei is only a splinter from the Mesbahiyeh sect. The problem is still Mesbah. They ruined the gatherings, the same ruining they did to TV. The gatherings have become empty, for the same reason that Friday prayers have become empty. There is a big difference between Taleghani and Alamolhoda, and it is very important whether the speaker is a great Beheshti or small Mesbahists... 9 Mehr 1405 https://t.me/hoseinghadyani
